Q002.covers: Uses the 28-day mean forecast as a labelled stand-in for unrecorded demand and recorded sales as the only observed fulfilment; true lost sales (demand that found an empty shelf) are not recorded, and this gap is not proof of a lost sale.

plans.covers: Recorded June 2026 sales of toned milk 500 ml (units and revenue) are the only observable evidence; true demand and lost sales from out-of-stock periods are not recorded, so this plan reports actual sales as a labelled stand-in and does not estimate the counterfactual.

Records the 11:00 shelf-audit snapshots where toned milk was empty; it does not record what shoppers actually bought instead, so substitution must be inferred from recorded sales of other products around those times.

Q005.covers: Counts distinct bills with an approved payment per day as a proxy for daily visitors; actual shopper/people visits are not recorded, and bills are not shoppers.

Q006.covers: Counts bills with a failed or failed: no response till payment attempt in June 2026 as a labelled stand-in for baskets abandoned at the till; actual shopper abandonment is not recorded, and a bill is not a shopper.

plans.covers: Uses each approved June UPI payment's bill_id as a labelled stand-in for a shopper (basket_value/shopper_count proxy) and sums approved payment amounts per bill to rank bills by spend; no customer identity is recorded, so actual people or households cannot be identified, and bills cover only the eleven followed items' approved payments.

Uses a bill as the stand-in for a shopper (shopper_count proxy) and checks whether the same bill contains atta, oil and dal among the eleven followed items; no record identifies actual shoppers or links them across bills, and bills outside the eleven followed items are not covered.

Counts and total rupees of recorded debit complaints (2026-06-04 to 2026-06-26) as the only recorded evidence of dissatisfaction; no customer satisfaction score, survey, sentiment, or customer identity is recorded.
Breakdown of recorded complaints by kind (charged twice; debited but the till said failed) as complaint evidence; the records hold no direct satisfaction measure or customer identity.

Breakdown of recorded complaints by recorded resolution (bank returned the money; refunded after the store matched the credit by hand) as evidence of how complaints were handled; no satisfaction rating or customer identity is recorded.

Approved June bills and their total approved payment value as the recorded volume of completed transactions (a bill stands in for a shopper, not a satisfaction score); customer satisfaction itself is not recorded.

Q011.cannot: The records cover only eleven followed items, and no snacks product is among them; there is no snacks-category field or category table, so no recorded evidence or labelled stand-in can assess how the snacks category is doing.

plans.covers: Recorded daily units and revenue for the eleven followed items are the only evidence available; the records do not identify a product launch, its date, or any causal substitution of one product's sales for another's, so this plan supplies the sales evidence only and cannot establish that a launch caused a decline in an existing product.
Recorded sales for the eleven followed items are used as the only demand proxy; actual shopper demand, shoppers who did not buy, and products outside these eleven are not recorded.
Recorded forecasts and ordered units are used as supply-side evidence; forecasts predict demand but demand itself is not recorded, so they cannot be scored against true demand.
Recorded damaged and expired write-offs are used as waste evidence; the underlying cause of each write-off and the shelf time lost to out-of-stock are not recorded.
Product identity, pack size, flow and list price/cost are recorded for the eleven products; real margins, competitor context and anything outside these eleven products are not recorded.
